symptom: `mxcli new`'s final settle build (and `mxcli docker build`) could hang indefinitely — observed 10+ minutes on macOS with Gradle at 100% CPU and no output, and nothing ever reported or gave up
cause: `SettleGeneratedSources` and `mxbuildCmd` called `cmd.Run()` bare: no deadline, no detection of a build that had stopped printing, and killing only the direct child would not have helped since mxbuild is a wrapper whose JVM/Gradle grandchildren hold the output pipe
insight: Bound the process TREE, not the child: the fake mxbuild in the test is `echo; sleep 60 & wait`, because a grandchild holding the pipe is exactly what makes `Wait` block after a plain Kill — reuse `setProcessGroup`/`killProcessGroup` and set `cmd.WaitDelay` as a backstop. The error carries the last output lines and the java home used, since a wrong --java-home was the cause the one time this was seen. Revert proof: `mxbuildCmd` with bare `cmd.Run()` leaves the hung fake running past the test's 20s guard. The trigger here was the /usr/bin/java stub (sibling finding); the watchdog is what turns the next unknown cause into an error instead of a hang
